Features include growth failure, relative macrocephaly, hypotonia, small hands/feet, feeding issues, precocious puberty, and mild developmental delay.

2. Wiedemann–Steiner syndrome  
Characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, distinctive facial features (prominent forehead, broad nasal tip), short stature/growth failure, hyperextensible joints, and small hands/feet; precocious puberty has been reported.

3. Floating-Harbor syndrome  
Presents with short stature, delayed speech/language, characteristic facial features (prominent forehead, broad nasal tip), small hands, and mild intellectual disability.

4. Coffin-Lowry syndrome  
Includes psychomotor delay, hypotonia, distinctive facies, joint laxity, and small hands; can have growth issues, though precocious puberty is less typical and disease is usually X-linked affecting males more severely.

5. Russell–Silver syndrome  
Marked by prenatal/postnatal growth failure, relative macrocephaly, triangular/prominent forehead, feeding difficulties, and sometimes small hands/feet; developmental delay is variable and precocious puberty can occur.
